critique: The timing is now convincingly flash-like: the burst is bright at 0.01 and completely gone by 0.08. The color is also much closer to a hot ignition. However, the visible flash still reads as a dense pile of overlapping, soft circular particles. It has no distinct near-white ignition point and too little directional separation to resemble the preset thumbnail's sharp, forceful muzzle-blast/starburst silhouette.

suggestions.why: Narrow the emission cone so the burst forms a deliberate forward muzzle direction instead of a rounded all-over cluster.
Push particles farther apart during the very short visible lifetime, creating an explosive directional silhouette and fragment separation.
Replace the large overlapping disc/blob appearance with smaller, sharper high-energy particles.
Collapse the large emitter volume toward a muzzle point so the burst originates from a concentrated hot center.
Raise the main particle color toward near-white yellow to establish a hotter ignition core rather than a uniformly orange-yellow cloud.
